chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Faddal, from Ibn Bukayr, from a man from our companions, from a man who said:

I said to Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him): I said to my wife, 'You are upon me like the back of my mother,' if you go out from the door of the room. She went out. He said to me, 'There is nothing upon you.' I said, 'I am capable of expiating.' He said, 'There is nothing upon you.' I said, 'I am capable of expiating a slave and two slaves.' He said, 'There is nothing upon you, whether you are capable or not.'

key_terms.الظِّهَار: Zihar, a form of divorce where a husband declares his wife unlawful to him by comparing her back to his mother's back

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on Zihar if the specific conditions are not met?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Rida (AS) clarifies that the specific condition of exiting through the 'door of the chamber' was not met, rendering the Zihar declaration inoperative and thus exempting the husband from expiation. This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise linguistic conditions in marital jurisprudence, where the Imam’s repeated reassurance underscores that the obligation is tied strictly to the completed act rather than the husband's capacity to perform it.
